pageCache.pageTitle: Buckland Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Small school, big hearts
Responsible
Buckland Church of England Primary School
We are very proud to be an outstanding school. Buckland has a long tradition of high academic achievement, exceptional levels of pastoral care and an imaginative programme of enrichment activities. “Spirituality, social responsibility and a very strong code of ethics permeates the school” and we offer “very effective teaching with a relentless focus on making sure each pupil is developed, nurtured and challenged.” (Ofsted 2016). Please make time to come and visit – our ethos is tangible. And our children really do enjoy life in all its fullness.
Our Church School
Wise, Responsible, Kind
We are a caring, village school which promotes Christian values, where each child receives a high standard of education that is broad, challenging, exciting and encourages creative thinking. We encourage every learner to be the best they can be, to reflect and plan the next steps in their learning journey, demonstrating a respect towards others and contributing to the communities of which they are a part.

pageCache.pageTitle: Buckland Church of England Primary School - Science Fair finals
pageCache.text:
Science Fair finals
On Wednesday 4th March, the winning pairs from Beech, Sycamore and Oak went to the Cambrian Learning Trust Science Fair final, held at The Elms school. The children each had the chance to present their own experiments to the panel of three judges and did an excellent job of answering questions and demonstrating their scientific knowledge. They also enjoyed different experiments led by students from FCC, as well as made an air vortex from a paper cup and balloon! All the children did fantastically well but special mention goes to Bertie and Axel from Oak class who came away with first place in the Year 5/6 competition for their experiment demonstrating the effect of UV light on bananas!

pageCache.pageTitle: Buckland Church of England Primary School - Afterschool Clubs

Afterschool Clubs
We offer a wide range of extra-curricular activities which prove to be extremely popular with our children. We encourage all children to take part in at least one enrichment activity as we believe it inspires learning, offers challenge and is an important part of emotional and social personal development.
Recent activities include: Football, Netball, Athletics, Choir, Arts and Crafts, Lego, Tennis and Science club.
A programme is created each term for children to choose from. Some activities are free, whilst others are provided through external companies and are booked and paid for directly. All external providers are quality assured by school staff and safeguarding expectations are the same as for everyone working in our school.
The vast majority of activities are available for all children and we can subsidise any child wishing to take part in a paid for activity. From time to time, there are activities which offer opportunities for children to compete or perform at a high level and in these circumstances fair selection criteria are applied.

pageCache.pageTitle: Buckland Church of England Primary School - Rights Respecting Schools Award
pageCache.text:
Rights Respecting Schools Award
'We did not come here to fear the future. We came here to shape it.' - Barack Obama
We were delighted to receive our Rights Respecting Silver award in July 2023. The assessor was very impressed with how confidently the children articulated their knowledge and understanding of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Here are some examples from the report:
The curriculum gives opportunities for children to find out about rights and a key stage two pupil explained that “It’s a key part of our school, it’s in history, RE, Tuesday assemblies and even in our guided reading. When asked to say more about how it linked to guided reading, he explained that in a text that they are reading, “It mentions freedom, and so they are not accessing their rights and it’s important to speak out and fight back.”
Children knew and understood that not all children in the United Kingdom were not able to access their rights and gave examples such as those “Living in an environment that is not safe for them,” and “Being abused or not listened to because of their skin colour or religion.”
It was evident that children benefited from understanding how rights and respect supported good relationships which contributes to pupils’ enjoyment of school; one child explained that “There’s always people who care, teachers will always find someone to sit with you and sometimes you don’t have to, because people will just come up to you.”
If you would like to read the whole report - please see below.
We are now continuing on our Rights Respecting Schools Award journey - working towards our Gold award. Over 1.5 million children in the UK attend a Rights Respecting School and nearly 5,000 schools up and down the country are working through the Award - using the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) as their guide. The Rights Respecting Schools Award helps schools to embed the values of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) in daily school life - it is based on principles of equality, dignity, respect, non-discrimination and participation - the UNCRC aligns very well with our school's vision and values, as well as our work on equality and diversity across the school. RRSA encourages children to become outward looking, responsible, active citizens.
There are 3 strands to the Rights Respecting Schools work -
For examples of work we have done towards each strand, please see the presentation - Buckland School's Journey to Silver.

Meet the Governors
'Governance is excellent. Governors meticulously ensure that pupils have all their needs fully met and no one is left behind. They champion the school because they assiduously check it is as good as it can be.' Ofsted, 2016
On this page you will find details of the names and terms of office for all of our Governors, together with details of their category of Governor, positions of responsibility and details of any additional committees that they serve on. We have also included details of the business and financial interests of each Governor and information about any Governance role they play in other schools, as well as a full breakdown of the structure and responsibilities of the governing body of our school and its committees. All governors sit on the local governing committee (LGC), each governor then sits on either the resources or quality of education committees. The pay committee meets once per year and is usually made up of some or all of the resources committee.
To contact the governors please email: kedavis@buc.cambrianlt.org
The Board of Trustees at Cambrian Learning Trust
The structure and remit of the CLT Members, Trustees, and its committees including the LGCs is available on the Trust website and can be found here >

I believe that love, kindness and connection must come first – when children feel safe, valued and understood, they can truly flourish. Our school is a warm, inclusive and ambitious community where high-quality teaching, curiosity and creativity go hand in hand. pageCache.pageTitle: Buckland Church of England Primary School - SEND and Inclusion
pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion
'Staff carefully track and support the achievement of disadvantaged pupils and pupils who have special educational needs and/or disabilities so they make the same strong progress as their peers.' Ofsted, 2016
Buckland is an inclusive mainstream academy school. Our aim for pupils who have been identified as having SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities), is to ensure that they are supported whilst also making sure they are fully included in the life of the school.
Buckland School provides additional help, support and guidance to children and young people with a wide range of SEND including those with:
Our SEND children are fully integrated into our four classes with small group spaces used for specific provision and support.
Early identification of SEND is vital to ensuring positive outcomes for pupils. We follow guidance from the Oxfordshire County Council publication, Identifying and Supporting Special Educational Needs in Oxfordshire Schools and Settings and the 2015, Special Educational Needs and Disability Code of Practice: 0–25 Years, when identifying and supporting pupils with SEND.
Through quality first and adaptive teaching, we do our utmost to ensure that pupils' needs are met in the mainstream classroom, wherever possible, so that pupils can learn and make good progress in school. Staff employ carefully planned strategies to support each individual student, including access to specific resources and additional training when needed.
We also have excellent links with outside agencies who further support and advise on our provision for pupils. These include: Educational Psychology Service, Speech and Language Therapy Service, Communication and Interaction Service, Autism Support, Young People’s Mental Health Services (CYPMHS), Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), Children’s Social Care (LCSS), The Mulberry Bush Outreach Service, SENDIASS Parent Partnership Service and the Advisory Team for Inclusion and Early Years Inclusion.
All mainstream schools have a Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator (SENDCo). They work with pupils, staff and parents to support pupils who need extra help to achieve their full potential at school.
Our SENDCo is Miss Kim Hatton. Should you have any queries please contact kihatton@buc.cambrianlt.org
Our Headteacher is Mrs Emma Brown. You can also address any queries by contacting embrown@buc.cambrianlt.org
Our governor with responsibility for SEND is Mrs Mary Lines.

pageCache.pageTitle: Buckland Church of England Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
A new National Curriculum for schools was introduced by the government in 2014. On this page you will find details of the curriculum that our school uses and the content of this for each subject within each academic year group. You will also find details of our phonics and reading scheme used. If you would like further information, please contact the school.
'Teaching, learning and assessment are highly effective. Pupils learn very well, show high levels of intellectual curiosity and are both challenged and stimulated by the work teachers set for them.' Ofsted, 2016
Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum is designed around our Christian values. Each term, we focus on 3 values across the school and develop a working understanding of them through our choice of texts and foundation subject learning, embedding reading and maths at the core. Our approach is to deliver knowledge rich, sequential learning which excites and inspires, provides opportunity for recap and challenge, raises questions for debate, develops learners’ confidence and enables independent learning to flourish. High standards, collaboration and valuing individuals’ well-being is at the heart of this process. We believe that how we teach is as important as what we teach and that enrichment experiences are an entitlement. We want our curriculum to enable our children to be wise, responsible and kind in line with our school core values.
Curriculum policies are available on our policies page.

Buckland Nursery
'Children get off to an incredibly strong start in the early years. They start learning to read quickly and also develop a secure understanding of numbers. Staff get to know children swiftly and check their progress in all areas of their learning. This means staff accurately identify any additional needs children have and put the right adjustments in place to make sure all children keep up.' Ofsted, 2022
In September 2014, we opened as Buckland Nursery. Previously known as Buckland Pre-school (established in 2003), the setting achieved an Outstanding OFSTED rating in March 2011. Our nursery continues to deliver high-quality provision and is further enhanced as a seamless and integral part of Buckland School, which was awarded Outstanding OFSTED status in October 2016 and again in 2022.
Buckland Nursery forms part of Acorn Class, which includes Foundation Stage children across two age groups: Reception (F1) and Nursery (F2). Both age groups learn together within one integrated classroom. This unique setting offers Nursery children an early experience of school life, supported by an experienced teacher and a dedicated team of support staff. Nursery provision operates at a ratio of 1:8.
Children who spend a year as F2 learners in Acorns are able to transition smoothly into F1 and full-time school life as a result of this unique setting. They benefit greatly from starting their school journey as confident, happy and well-prepared learners.
Although we are unable to guarantee school places for Nursery children, as admissions are managed by the local authority on behalf of the Cambrian Learning Trust, we actively support all applications from families whose children have attended the Nursery. Buckland Nursery children are also given priority over applicants applying solely on the basis of distance.
Admissions
Admissions for Buckland Nursery are managed internally in line with the criteria set out in our admissions policy (see below). As outlined in our school admissions policy, attending our nursery provides children with an advantage when applying for a Reception place. Nursery children are considered after applicants living outside the catchment area without a sibling at the school, but before those whose applications are considered solely on the basis of distance. As we offer 11 Nursery places and have 15 Reception places available, this arrangement should enable all of our Nursery children to be offered a place in Reception at our school.
Please see below for the expression of interest form to apply for a nursery place.
Should you wish to visit the nursery setting please contact the office on 01367 870236.
Location
Buckland School is both fortunate in its location and wealth of facilities. Buckland is a small village with no major roads and surrounded by beautiful countryside. The village has a local church and a large village hall. Buckland School is able to enjoy these facilities for many activities such as school productions, special events and swimming lessons in the summer term. Buckland School itself has a large outdoor play area, including a playground, grassed areas and a quiet garden. In addition, the Nursery and Reception children have their own fenced and secure play area laid on an all-weather surface where they are able to experience a varied outdoor curriculum. In this play area, the children can play in sand, in the outdoor summer house, on a climbing frame and with wheeled vehicles. The classroom is well-equipped to provide a challenging range of activities. A recent addition is a covered decking area which enables us to provide outdoor play in all weathers.
Curriculum
Nursery teaching is based on the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum, with a strong emphasis on hands-on, practical experiences linked to each term’s topic. Our topics follow the school’s rolling two-year cycle but are carefully adapted to reflect the needs and interests of our youngest learners. Recent topics have included: Amazing Acorns, Once Upon A Time, Where in the World, Animal Adventures and Watch Us Grow. Children learn alongside our reception children. We make full use of our outdoor environment, which is an extension of our classroom, and also enjoy Forest School sessions. To enrich our learning further, we welcome a range of visitors into our setting, including Little City, Zoolab and Emergency Services teams.
Funding and Lunch club
Nursery children may attend for either a 15-hour place (9:00am–12:00pm, five days per week – up to 11 places) or a 30-hour place (9:00am–3:00pm, five days per week – up to 8 places) during term time. Once a place is accepted, it must be taken as the full 15 or 30 hours, as these sessions cannot be reallocated to another child. We also ask for consistent attendance so that staff know who to expect and children can establish secure routines.
Families may choose to use their 15-hour morning place with us and arrange alternative afternoon provision elsewhere, effectively splitting the 30 hours between settings. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer afternoon-only places or full-day 15-hour places.
Children who are not eligible for funded hours and attend on a private basis will be charged £5.70 per hour. Please note that this rate is reviewed annually.
There are 8 Nursery lunch club places available for children attending the 30-hour provision. Children may choose either a hot school dinner or bring their own packed lunch.
